name: Dashboarding Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for dashboarding work: a short set of checks to run before calling a dashboarding task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for dashboarding work: a short set of checks to run before calling a dashboarding task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to dashboarding (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. Measure before optimizing any dashboarding bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. When dashboarding decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. Check that dashboarding terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
5. Before starting dashboarding work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. When multiple dashboarding strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. Keep dashboarding changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
8. Keep dashboarding outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
9. When dashboarding guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop dashboarding edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting dashboarding assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new dashboarding abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated dashboarding concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of dashboarding correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these dashboarding guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
